history.period: Foundation stone laid 1916 CE; temple established 1917 CE (Vikram Samvat 1974); Ghantakarna shrine installed 1918/1923 per varying accounts (verify)
history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN (SVETAMBARA) TIRTH, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Mahudi Jain Temple at Mahudi town, Mansa taluka, Gandhinagar district, is a pilgrimage centre for Svetambara Jains and devotees of all communities. The modern temple was established by Svetambara Jain monk Buddhisagarsuri: the foundation stone was laid in 1916 on land donated by Vadilal Kalidas Vora, and the temple with a 22-inch white marble idol of Padmaprabh (the 6th Tirthankara) was established in 1917 CE (Maghsar Sudi 6, VS 1974). The separate shrine of Ghantakarna Mahavir - a protector deity shown holding a bow and arrow (unusual for Jainism's ahimsa), said to have been King Tungabhadra in a previous birth - was installed later; sources differ between VS 1980/1923 CE and 1918 (verify). A Guru Mandir dedicated to Buddhisagarsuri was added later. The site was historically known as Madhupuri/Madhumati, on the banks of the Madhumati river; Brahmi-script inscriptions and excavated idols suggest antiquity of ~2000 years. The signature custom: devotees offer sukhadi (wheat-flour-jaggery-ghee sweet) to Ghantakarna Mahavir and must consume it within the temple complex - it may not be carried out. Every year on Kali Chaudas, lakhs attend the Havan; devotees climb a ladder to ring the tall bell and make wishes. OPENING HOURS NOTE: yatradham and adinathtravels agree on 6:00 AM-8:00 PM with morning aarti 6 AM and evening aarti 7-8 PM; place listings vary (7 AM-7 PM, 6 AM-9:30 PM) - verify. Coordinates from mahudi.org place data, approximate.

name: Shri Ghantakarna Mahavir Jain Temple (Mahudi Jain Tirth)
town: Mahudi (CSV town 'Gandhinagar' is the district/city - the tirth is at Mahudi town, Mansa taluka, ~35 km from Gandhinagar)
town_description: Mahudi is a town in Mansa taluka of Gandhinagar district, situated on the banks of the Madhumati river, a tributary of the Sabarmati. Historically known as Madhupuri (or Madhumati), it is an ancient settlement with Brahmi inscriptions and excavated idols pointing to ~2000 years of habitation. It is a major Jain pilgrimage centre for the Ghantakarna Mahavir shrine, drawing devotees of all communities, and lies about 35 km from Gandhinagar and 65-70 km from Ahmedabad.

travel.airport: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport, Ahmedabad, ~60-65 km
travel.railway: Vijapur railway station, ~10 km (nearest); Gandhinagar railway station, ~40 km (verify)
travel.road: Direct buses from Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar and Kalol; Mahudi bus stop ~230 m from the temple; temple complex has dharamshala and bhojanalaya

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Kali Chaudas (October-November) is the biggest festival - expect very heavy crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM - 8:00 PM daily; morning aarti 6:00 AM, evening aarti 7:00-8:00 PM (verify - some place listings give 7:00 AM-7:00 PM or 6:00 AM-9:30 PM); sukhadi prasad must be consumed within the complex, not taken out; photography not allowed per yatradham
